newsitem.title: USA: Late Brent crude trade in U.S. deflates prices.
newsitem.headline: Late Brent crude trade in U.S. deflates prices.

text.p: Lackluster dealings in the North Sea paper Brent market left prices weaker Tuesday afternoon, foreign crude traders said.
A small number of partial trades were seen for May Brent. Deals were done as weak as $20.12, some 16 cents lower than the IPE settlement price for May futures at $20.28 per barrel.
A total of 500 lots were sold at $20.15 in two separate deals, with another 200 lots moved at $20.17.
Inter-month Brent spreads were as quiet as the outrights, with the only confirmed trade a May/June spread at +15 cts, some 5 cts higher than previous markings.
